agents.name: Sunitinib
agents.type: Oral targeted therapy: tyrosine kinase inhibitor
agents.explanation: Sunitinib blocks several kinases, including KIT and blood-vessel growth receptors. After imatinib resistance or intolerance it may slow gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST) growth. Its effects on normal blood vessels and other tissues explain the need for blood-pressure, heart, thyroid and organ-function monitoring.
agents.watch: Report painful hands or feet, worsening diarrhoea, bleeding, chest pain, breathlessness, faintness, severe headache or a blistering rash promptly. Do not restart after a serious reaction without oncology review.
risks: Fatigue, appetite or taste change, nausea, diarrhoea and mouth soreness
Painful hand-foot skin reaction, skin or hair colour changes and rash
High blood pressure, thyroid dysfunction and low blood counts
Serious liver injury, heart weakness or rhythm problems, bleeding or blood clots
Rare bowel perforation, pancreatic inflammation, severe skin reactions, neurological syndromes or kidney injury/protein loss, including small-vessel clotting
Impaired wound healing and jaw-bone injury (osteonecrosis); fertility/pregnancy harm
Rare severe infection, low blood glucose or brain effects causing unexplained confusion, seizures or visual change

anatomy: Severe headache, confusion, seizures or new visual problems can signal serious blood-pressure or brain effects. Seek urgent help.
Soreness and taste change can reduce intake. Use gentle mouth care and ask for symptom support early.
Attend blood-pressure checks. Chest pain, new breathlessness, fainting or severe palpitations needs urgent assessment.
Liver injury can occur without early symptoms. Keep blood-test appointments and report yellow eyes or dark urine.
Report reduced urine, swelling or dehydration. Your team checks kidney function and may check urine protein when indicated.
Report fever, sudden illness, unusual bruising or bleeding. Heavy bleeding, black stools or coughing blood needs urgent help.
Ask early about diarrhoea. Severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting or inability to drink requires urgent advice.
Report soreness, redness, cracks or blisters early. Reduce rubbing and heat and follow the skin-care plan.

monitoring_schedule.note: Safety testing and tumour-response assessment answer different questions.

monitoring_test_details.label: Full blood count
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Detect infection, anaemia and bleeding risk.
monitoring_test_details.timing: At baseline and before each cycle.

monitoring_test_details.label: Kidney and liver tests
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Detect organ effects and guide treatment review.
monitoring_test_details.timing: At baseline and before each cycle. Repeat sooner for symptoms or abnormal results.

monitoring_test_details.label: Thyroid function
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Identify underactive or overactive thyroid function, which may need treatment.
monitoring_test_details.timing: At baseline and every 12 weeks under this National Cancer Control Programme source; sooner if symptoms suggest a thyroid problem.

monitoring_test_details.label: Blood pressure
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Detect high blood pressure even before symptoms occur.
monitoring_test_details.timing: At baseline and each attendance; additional home or clinic checks as prescribed.

monitoring_test_details.label: Heart function and rhythm
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Identify heart weakness or electrical-rhythm risk.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Review cardiac history and whether electrocardiogram (heart tracing), echocardiogram (heart ultrasound) or multigated acquisition scan (heart pumping scan) are indicated; further assessment follows risk, symptoms or abnormal findings. Electrolytes and medicines that affect the QT electrical recovery interval are reviewed when relevant.

monitoring_test_details.label: Urine protein
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Detect protein leakage and kidney complications.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Product information supports baseline urine testing and monitoring for protein loss during treatment; the team specifies repeat timing.

monitoring_test_details.label: Blood glucose in people with diabetes
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Detect low glucose and review diabetes medicines.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Check regularly if diabetes is present and promptly with symptoms suggesting low glucose.

monitoring_test_details.label: Mouth, dental health, skin and wound review
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Identify hand–foot effects, mouth problems or healing concerns early.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Review symptoms throughout treatment; consider dental assessment before treatment and coordinate surgery or invasive dental care with oncology.

monitoring_test_details.label: Tumour response review
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Assess benefit separately from treatment-safety tests.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Your gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST) specialist sets imaging and clinical-review timing. This advanced-disease plan assesses tumour control, symptoms and whether treatment remains useful.

support.title: Preparation and support medicines
support.text: Confirm the exact calendar and dose strength before each cycle. Review all prescription, non-prescription and herbal products, especially the liver enzyme cytochrome P450 3A4 interactions; avoid grapefruit and St John’s wort. Keep a blood-pressure and symptom record if your team asks. No routine separate premedication is specified. This oral schedule has minimal-to-low emetogenic potential; symptom medicines are prescribed individually. Ask for a hand-foot skin-care plan and early diarrhoea support. Treat blood-pressure or thyroid problems as prescribed. Tell the team before surgery, dental procedures or starting any new medicine.

support.title: Oral medicine handling
support.text: Keep tablets or capsules in their supplied packaging, away from children, and follow the pharmacy storage instructions. Do not share medicines or alter the dose yourself. Ask the pharmacy before crushing, opening or dispersing a medicine; formulation-specific instructions differ. Return unused treatment to the pharmacy.

support.title: Fertility and pregnancy precautions
support.text: Discuss fertility, effective contraception, pregnancy prevention and breastfeeding before treatment. Your team must give the product-specific precautions and duration for you and your partner. Tell oncology promptly about a possible pregnancy.

support.title: Your wider treatment plan
support.text: gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST) is a distinct tumour type. A specialist team reviews pathology, KIT/platelet-derived growth factor receptor alpha and other relevant molecular findings, prior treatment, symptoms and scans. Surgery may be appropriate for resectable disease or selected situations. Radiotherapy has a selective role, rather than being a routine partner to these tablets. Nutrition, symptom control and supportive or palliative care can be used alongside active cancer treatment.

support.title: Missed or vomited doses
support.text: Skip a missed sunitinib dose and take the next scheduled dose at the usual time. Do not take an extra or double dose. Ask the team about vomiting or repeated missed doses.

evidence.title: Randomised sunitinib trial after imatinib failure in gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST)
evidence.summary: A placebo-controlled trial showed that sunitinib delayed gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST) progression after imatinib resistance or intolerance. The studied schedule was 50 mg daily for four weeks followed by two weeks off.
evidence.intro: A placebo-controlled trial showed that sunitinib delayed gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST) progression after imatinib resistance or intolerance. The studied schedule was 50 mg daily for four weeks followed by two weeks off.
evidence.caveat: Trial findings apply to previously treated gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST) and the studied schedule. They do not predict an individual response or establish benefit in renal cancer, another treatment line or the alternative 21-day calendar.
evidence.interpretation: Trial findings apply to previously treated gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST) and the studied schedule. They do not predict an individual response or establish benefit in renal cancer, another treatment line or the alternative 21-day calendar.

questions.q: What is the treatment trying to do?
questions.a: Sunitinib aims to slow gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST) growth and help symptoms after imatinib has stopped working or cannot be tolerated. The team reviews previous treatment, tumour biology, your health and priorities before choosing the schedule. GIST is a distinct tumour type. A specialist team reviews pathology, KIT/platelet-derived growth factor receptor alpha and other relevant molecular findings, prior treatment, symptoms and scans. Surgery may be appropriate for resectable disease or selected situations. Radiotherapy has a selective role, rather than being a routine partner to these tablets. Nutrition, symptom control and supportive or palliative care can be used alongside active cancer treatment.

National Cancer Control Programme 00325: sunitinib 50 mg by mouth once daily on days 1–28, followed by 14 days without sunitinib. Repeat the 42-day cycle only as confirmed by your team. Dose reductions or additional holds may be needed; symptoms and monitoring continue during the planned break.

questions.q: Does a delay mean treatment has failed?
questions.a: No. Blood counts, organ function and symptoms can make a delay or dose change safer. Your team decides whether and when to give the next dose.

questions.q: Who do I contact if unwell?
questions.a: Use your verified oncology daytime or out-of-hours number. If you cannot reach the team, seek urgent medical assessment. Severe symptoms require 112/999.

questions.q: What should I do about a missed or vomited dose?
questions.a: Skip a missed sunitinib dose and take the next scheduled dose at the usual time. Do not take an extra or double dose. Ask the team about vomiting or repeated missed doses.

questions.q: Can I take other medicines or supplements?
questions.a: Confirm the exact calendar and dose strength before each cycle. Review all prescription, non-prescription and herbal products, especially the liver enzyme cytochrome P450 3A4 interactions; avoid grapefruit and St John’s wort. Keep a blood-pressure and symptom record if your team asks.

questions.q: Why do I need checks if I feel well?
questions.a: High blood pressure, thyroid changes, liver injury or low blood counts may be detected before you notice symptoms. The required checks differ by medicine; keep your individual schedule.
